The issue is that `ChatMessage` currently reads `agentSeed` by matching the item's author ID against available agents, but for helper threads the author is the parent agent (like Bubbles) rather than the helper itself (like Copy). Jamel wants the helper's name and mark to be used instead. I'm weighing two approaches: either add a helper field directly to `ThreadItem` so `ChatMessage` can render the `SubagentMark` when present, or have `buildThread` accept an optional identity override that applies the helper name and mark to all agent-authored items in that thread. The second option feels cleaner since it's a single configuration point, and only `SubagentRun` would need to pass this override. But there's a subtlety—the helper's thread also contains the person's own messages if they steer via the composer, and those should stay attributed to the person, not the helper. Only agent-authored items like replies, thinking, and tool calls should get the helper identity, while note items stay as crew.

Keeping it simple might mean not wrapping it in `MemberName` when it's a helper.

Looking at the design rules, agents always render their deterministic generated pet icon, never an avatar. A helper is different and should get its own generated mark. So the approach is to add a `helperSeed` field to `ThreadItem`, and when it's set, `ChatMessage` draws the helper mark instead of the agent icon, with the name rendered plain text rather than wrapped in `MemberName`. The `-ml-2` negative margin shifts it left by 8px, but that doesn't solve the core issue: if the button's minimum content width exceeds the available space after accounting for the padding, `max-width` won't force it to shrink below that minimum.

A block child with negative left margin inside a scroller creates an interesting situation: the scrollable overflow region doesn't include content overflowing on the start side (it just clips), but with `max-w-full` on the button, its max-width is 100% of the parent's content width, and starting at -8px means it extends further than expected.

I'm second-guessing whether I should've changed `openSubagent` to reuse the parent's tab instead of looking for an already-open tab showing that specific helper. The old behavior would find a tab with a matching threadId and bring it forward, or create a new one if needed—so opening different helpers would spawn separate tabs. But now I'm not sure if that's the right approach based on what I documented in AGENTS.md about tabs being closable and allowing multiple instances.

There's a real design tension here: `showSubagents` reuses tabs by `parentThreadId`, and the back button in the panel converts a helper tab back into the list by clearing the threadId. So the tab already operates as "one tab per parent thread, navigating between list and helper views." Under my old code, opening a second helper while one was open would create a second tab with the same parentThreadId, which `showSubagents` would then find inconsistently. My change makes this coherent—one helpers tab per thread, navigating between the list and whichever helper is active, matching the panel's two-screen design and the toggle button I'm adding. But I'm losing the ability to have several helpers open at once, and I'm not sure if that's a regression the user would actually notice or care about.

With chips in the thread, clicking helper A then helper B just replaces the view rather than opening two tabs side by side. You can't watch two at once anyway since there's only one panel. Tabs let you flip between them, but the list screen does that in one press. I think one tab per thread is simpler and makes the header toggle honest, but it does change behavior beyond what was asked. The safer approach would be to keep the "one tab per helper" behavior but record the parent so the toggle can find it—but then `closeSubagents` becomes ambiguous if there are several tabs. A toggle whose "off" state is unclear isn't simple. Maybe the button shouldn't be a toggle at all; the plan and board buttons toggle because those are pinned singular tabs, but helpers is just an ordinary tab. A simpler behavior might be to have the button just open the helpers tab rather than toggle it. I need to verify that closing tabs works correctly and that `closeSubagents` does what I expect.
